newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian tax service chief offers to quit - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Russian tax service chief offers to quit - Interfax.

text.p: The head of Russia's State Tax Service, Vitaly Artyukhov, has tendered his resignation to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, Interfax news agency said on Saturday, quoting a source close to the government.

A government reshuffle last month brought in more liberal reformers committed to increasing tax revenues. The government blames massive tax evasion for depriving it of the money to pay public sector workers, pensioners and welfare claimants.
Interfax said Artyukhov's offer to quit was probably connected to uncertainty surrounding a reorganisation of the tax service and his own personal future.

One of the promoted reformers, Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh, told a convention of Russian city mayors that tax collection in the first quarter was only 58 percent of the budgeted figure, Itar-Tass news agency reported.

Kokh called it "a crisis of statehood." He said Russia might ban alcohol imports as the evasion of alcohol duty, particularly through the smuggling of vodka from other former Soviet states, was one of the main causes of low government revenue.
The 20 biggest non-payers of tax -- effectively large corporations -- account for about 60 percent of the debts owed by the government, Kokh said, calling for tough measures against them.

Interfax said that since taking office 14 months ago Artyukhov had improved the collection of money from tax dodgers. It quoted "tax analysts" as saying his resignation, if accepted, could seriously disrupt his reorganisation of the tax service.
